chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was on a journey, and behold, there was an elderly man. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about a man who catches the Imam at Jam'?' He said to him: 'If he expects that he will reach 'Arafat and stand there for a short while, then catch Jam' before the sunrise, let him go to Jam'. And if he expects that he will not reach it until the people depart from Jam', then let him not go to it, for his Hajj is complete.'

key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', the station where the Prophet combined Dhuhr and Asr prayers during Hajj
key_terms.طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ: Sunrise, the time limit for the combined prayer at Jam'
key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: 'Arafat, the essential station of Hajj where the standing (wuquf) takes place
key_terms.يُفِيضَ النَّاسُ: The people depart/leave (referring to the departure of the congregation from Jam')

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who arrives late at Jam' and must choose between joining the Imam there or proceeding to 'Arafat?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* elucidates the principle of *al-ghabn* (reasonable expectation) in determining the validity of the essential pillar of standing at 'Arafat (*wuquf*) versus the recommended act of joining the Imam at Jam'. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ease (*rukhas*) and the flexibility of ritual timing, ensuring that a pilgrim does not miss the core obligation due to logistical constraints. The ruling underscores that while joining the Imam is highly meritorious, it does not invalidate Hajj if missed, provided the pilgrim secures the essential *wuquf* at 'Arafat.
